title: Rav Yehuda bar Yishmael
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Chullin 118b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.118b.8) in a halakhic discussion. It appears to Hyman that he is the one who is always called in the Yerushalmi by the name Rabbi Yudan bei Rabbi Yishmael.

Hyman describes him as a great man who maintained a great academy, citing [Yerushalmi Berakhot ch. 4, halakha 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.4.2.5): Rabbi Yudan bei Rabbi Yishmael instructed his public interpreter to recite after his exposition (the prayer of Rabbi Chiyya bar Vava) thus. Hyman cites [Berakhot 5:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.5.1.20) for the story in which he would meditate on words of Torah so intensely that his cloak fell off, and a snake guarded it so that no one else would take it; his students said to him, "Rabbi, here is your cloak lying on the ground." He said to them, "And is that wicked creature not careful about it?" And in [Jerusalem Talmud Nedarim 4:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Nedarim.4.3.3), he permitted teachers of children to take payment, and said that they take payment for lost time (from work). So it is also cited in [the Ran, Nedarim 36b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ran_on_Nedarim.36b.9.3). And in [Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 1:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.1.4.11), he said that the court disagreed with him (Rabbi Yehuda Nesia) concerning divorce. And there, [ch. 3, halakha 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.3.2.3), Rabbi Yudan bei Rabbi Yishmael ruled, because of pressure, to rake out an oven, etc. And there, [ch. 6, halakha 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.6.2.2), it is related that his foot was worn away from a wound and he put on a hobnailed sandal. And the view of Mavo HaYerushalmi is that he was the brother of Ulla (without further qualification) bar Yishmael.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The linked Berakhot 4:2 describes a public interpreter. In the bracketed reading of the linked 5:1, Yudan’s cloak falls unnoticed. The snake guarding the cloak and the exchange with the students belong to Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon. Hyman and [Heilprin’s notice](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1704&lang=en) relate the snake episode under Yudan.

The linked Nedarim and Ran explain that the payment covers lost time. The Shabbat 6:2 account specifies a patch beneath the hobnailed sandal. The identification of the Bavli’s Yehudah with Yudan, and the proposed brotherhood with Ulla, remain attributed to Hyman and his cited source, respectively.
